title: Copper Heads for Longest Weekly Losing Streak in Two Years | OilPrice.com

Nvidia (Nasdaq: NVDA) beat Wall Street’s revenue forecast by about $6.7 billion on Tuesday night, and copper fell for a fifth straight session on Wednesday.

Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 3.6% at $12,763 a metric ton in early London trading, according to Investing.com. Bloomberg had earlier reported a low of $13,019, the weakest since June 24, with the metal on course for its longest streak of weekly declines in two years.

Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue against the $109.1 billion analysts expected, according to LSEG data cited by Fox Business, and guided fiscal fourth-quarter sales to about $130 billion. It was the first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and Saxo Bank said the board does not intend to bring him back.

Tuesday’s tech rout pushed U.S. stocks to a fourth straight loss and Europe to its worst day since March, Saxo said. ING commodities strategist Ewa Manthey said the AI selloff has raised concerns about copper “given the metal’s growing exposure to investment in power grids and data centres.”

The dollar sits near a 19-month high, Reuters reported, and traders are waiting on the Federal Reserve’s October meeting minutes with more aggressive tightening already expected, Bloomberg said. TD Securities analysts added that U.S. tariffs on refined copper now look less likely, removing another source of support. The same rate worries pushed gold to a 14-month low near $3,780 an ounce, Saxo said.

The slide predates Huang’s exit, and it has left copper about 14% below its $14,875 record from September. Goldman Sachs has called it a matter of positioning in AI-linked stocks, not a sign that fundamentals have loosened, as Oilprice.com reported last week. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri said Nvidia has become a key source of funding for neoclouds and AI developers, and he expects it to pause those deals even if a new CEO holds the same course. A pause would push data center construction, and the copper that goes into it, further out.

Aluminum was down 0.9% at $2,907.50 a metric ton by early afternoon in Shanghai, Bloomberg said, a day after the metal touched its lowest in almost a year. That came even though the premium of the LME cash contract over the three-month contract hit its highest since 1988 on Monday on thin stocks before easing, Reuters reported Tuesday. Manthey said she expects “this tightness to continue supporting prices in the near term,” though stronger production growth should gradually improve availability further out.

Zinc lost 1% and tin 2% on the LME, Reuters reported, and nickel gave back part of Tuesday’s jump above its 200-day moving average. Chinese buyers, though, are paying a record premium to import copper, with the premium up 21% on Tuesday alone as inventories in the world’s top consumer run low. London is selling the same metal at its lowest price in nearly five months.
